name: The Climber's Cafe
why_it_matters: Tripadvisor #1 of 3 restaurants in Keylong with a perfect 5.0 rating. The town's only purpose-built cafe — owner Sunil Bodh runs the floor himself, the terrace looks straight onto snow-capped peaks above the Bhaga valley. The default Manali-Leh-highway pitstop for breakfast or coffee.
insider_tip: Order shapta and timo together — it's the Lahauli equivalent of stew-and-bread, almost never on the printed Indian-cuisine page. Open 7:45am, so a workable early start before the Baralacha or Atal Tunnel runs.
signature_address: Mall Road, Next To Canara Bank, Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Nordaling Garden Restaurant
signature_dish: veg and chicken momos with thukpa
why_it_matters: The Lonely Planet pick for Keylong — a small mood-lit garden eatery between apple trees and hollyhocks behind the Nordaling Guest House, five minutes' walk from the HRTC bus stand. Many vegetables and the apples for the juice come from the property's own organic garden. Tripadvisor's #1 guest house in Keylong with a 4.3/5 rating.
insider_tip: The fresh apple juice is unusual for the highway — most Lahaul stops only have packaged Tropicana. Ask at the guest-house reception if the garden is open; on warm afternoons they pull tables out under the trees.
signature_address: Near Bus Stand, Upper Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: The Chanderabhaga Restaurant (HPTDC)
why_it_matters: The state-government HPTDC property opposite the New Circuit House — operates June through October only, mirroring the Rohtang-Atal Tunnel-Baralacha-La access window. Plain veg-only canteen-style meals; the meaning lies in being a known, fixed waypoint where solo and family travellers can land a hot plate without a hotel reservation.
insider_tip: There is no menu — the kitchen serves what's been cooked that meal. Ring ahead on (01900) 222247 if arriving outside obvious lunch/dinner hours; the restaurant pace assumes resident guests, not walk-ins.
signature_address: The Chanderabhaga, Manali-Leh Road, Opp. New Circuit House, Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Hotel Tashi Delek Restaurant
why_it_matters: A 46-room Mall Road hotel that's the second-ranked stay in town — the in-house dining hall is one of the few Keylong rooms big enough for a tour bus to land at once, hence its place in fixed-itinerary Manali-Leh group menus. The apple pie is the dish guests repeat on TripAdvisor.
insider_tip: Pricier than the bazaar dhabas, but portion sizes are tour-group ample. If on a fixed-budget run from Manali, eat lighter items here and save the splurge for Climber's Cafe.
signature_address: The Mall, Main Bazaar, Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Hotel Gyespa Restaurant
why_it_matters: Lonely Planet flagged Gyespa's tree-fronted terrace as 'the most atmospheric dining experience on The Mall' — coloured lamps, blue gingham tablecloths, the only Keylong room that puts Israeli and Middle-Eastern items on the same card as Tibetan and Indian (the Manali backpacker-trail influence). 100m from the bus stand.
insider_tip: Service is famously slow — order, walk the bazaar for thirty minutes, return. The beer is sold but reviewers complain it's never properly cold; switch to chai if you actually want cold drink.
signature_address: Opposite Rasbihari Bose Chowk, Near Bus Stand, The Mall, Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132

name: Hotel Snow Land Restaurant
why_it_matters: A small budget-tier hotel kitchen that quietly runs Nepali-cooked food — chicken curry done as the kitchen knows it, not as the menu translates it. The cheapest verifiable hot meal in Keylong (rooms ₹500-1000), and the chef sources vegetables from local Keylong gardens.
insider_tip: Walk in at lunch and ask what the chef is cooking that day rather than ordering off the printed sheet. Vegetables on the plate change with whichever Lahauli garden delivered that morning.
signature_address: Old Circuit House Road, Manali-Leh Highway, Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh 175132
